segments.text: August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Aaron Booker

, a nonresident, criticized what he viewed as inconsistent enforcement of meeting decorum and a broader pattern of selective enforcement within the City and Police Department. He urged City officials to apply standards equally, protect First Amendment rights, and pursue meaningful reform.
View minutes, page 1
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Daniel Sroka

urged the City to take action to restore public trust in the Police Department, suggesting policy revisions, improved body cameras, or a resident review board. Citing public critiques of body-camera footage, Mr. Sroka called for meaningful reform and emphasized the importance of protecting constitutional rights.
View minutes, page 2
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Debbie Shaw

described her family’s longstanding service to American Fork and raised concerns about alleged civil-rights violations involving her son and others. She requested a fair, transparent, and independent review of the Police Department and urged City leadership to restore public trust through accountability and action.
View minutes, page 2
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Jan Chamberlain

, a member of the NO ICE in Utah County Coalition, requested a meeting with City officials to discuss immigration enforcement policies. She supported lawful due process while encouraging a humanitarian approach that protects innocent immigrants and children. She also asked the City to consider policies limiting the use of municipal property and local law-enforcement resources for federal immigration enforcement.
View minutes, page 2
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Mary Mitchell

an American Fork resident supported an independent review of the Police Department and urged the city to rebuild public trust, particularly among vulnerable and immigrant communities. She requested greater transparency regarding the Police Department’s cooperation with ICE under Utah County’s 287(g) Agreement, citing concerns about racial profiling and residents becoming afraid to contact law enforcement.
View minutes, page 2
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Roy Shaw

, an American Fork resident, requested an independent third-party review of the Police Department’s accountability, leadership, and handling of alleged misconduct. He stated that the review should determine whether systemic or leadership failures exist, restore public confidence, and guide any appropriate personnel action. He also expressed concern that similar requests from residents had received no meaningful response.
View minutes, page 2
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Andrea Tamita
, a 93-year-old American Fork citizen, urged City officials and residents to address wrongdoing, hold public officials and safety patrols accountable, and protect children.
View minutes, page 3
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Elizabeth Oscarson

, an American Fork resident, opposed ICE activity within the city and stated that residents deserve to feel safe. She requested complete transparency and public reporting regarding interactions between City departments and federal immigration authorities.
View minutes, page 3
August 25, 2026 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Gregory Titus
stated that his and his wife’s constitutional rights had been violated in American Fork. He expressed a willingness to work with City officials and invited them to contact him regarding his concerns.
View minutes, page 3
